title: Accelerator memory capacity vs context-window growth
bottleneck: Model context windows and parameter counts grow faster than accelerator memory capacity; a single GPU still can't hold frontier models, forcing complex tensor and pipeline parallelism with heavy communication overhead. HBM capacity per package grows slowly and expensively, while KV-cache for long contexts explodes memory demand at inference. Memory capacity, not FLOPS, increasingly decides which models can run where.
why_it_blocks: Capacity limits fragment models across many chips, raising latency, cost, and energy per token; long-context applications (agents, video, genomics) are throttled by what fits in memory. Progress in model capability outruns the hardware's ability to host it.
current_state: Larger HBM stacks, disaggregated memory pools, KV-cache compression, and sparsity techniques stretch capacity. The fundamental capacity-per-dollar trend still lags model growth.
